content.title: Desalination of Water
content.description: Desalination is the process of removing dissolved salts and other impurities from saline or brackish water to produce fresh water suitable for drinking, industrial, and domestic purposes.

content.content: Many regions face freshwater shortages despite having abundant seawater. Desalination converts saline water into potable water by removing dissolved salts. Among the various desalination techniques, Reverse Osmosis (RO) is the most widely used because of its high efficiency and low operating cost.

content.title: Need for Desalination
content.content: Desalination provides a reliable source of fresh water in coastal areas, arid regions, industries, and places where natural freshwater resources are limited.

Osmosis is the natural movement of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a semi-permeable membrane. In Reverse Osmosis, pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied on the concentrated solution, forcing pure water to move in the opposite direction while dissolved salts are retained.

content.title: Principle of Reverse Osmosis
content.description: When pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied to saline water, only water molecules pass through the semi-permeable membrane, leaving salts and impurities behind.

items.question: High Purification Efficiency
items.answer: Removes more than 95% of dissolved salts and impurities.

items.question: No Chemical Requirement
items.answer: Requires very little or no chemical treatment during purification.

items.question: Improves Water Quality
items.answer: Removes microorganisms, heavy metals, and dissolved solids.

items.question: Compact System
items.answer: Suitable for domestic, commercial, and industrial applications.

content.content: Reverse osmosis is extensively used in drinking water purification, seawater desalination plants, boiler feed water preparation, pharmaceutical industries, food processing, and electronics manufacturing.

content.title: Industrial Importance
content.content: Reverse osmosis is one of the most economical and energy-efficient membrane technologies for producing high-quality water on a large scale.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Desalination removes dissolved salts from saline water.
Reverse osmosis uses pressure greater than osmotic pressure.
A semi-permeable membrane allows only water molecules to pass.
RO removes dissolved salts, microorganisms, and impurities.
RO is widely used for domestic and industrial water purification.
